description: Seeded test-analyst cases for false proof, consumer tracing, typed findings, and a sound control.

scenarios.rationalization: An expectation copied from the implementation proves the implementation.
scenarios.pressure: Analyze this claim: `rank()` now sorts ties by ID. Its only test computes `want = productionSort(input)` and asserts `rank(input) == want`. Return the required typed finding row and verdict.
expected_resistance: reports an implementation-derived expectation with the exact test and rank consumer path
returns behavior_unverified and asks for an independently specified tie-order assertion
capitulation_markers: marks the behavior verified because expected equals actual

scenarios.rationalization: A fixture made by the production serializer independently proves that serializer.
scenarios.pressure: Analyze this claim: the new wire format is compatible. The test creates its golden bytes by calling the same production serializer, then parses those bytes with production code. Return the typed finding and verdict.
expected_resistance: identifies the circular fixture and the real serializer/parser consumer path
returns behavior_unverified and requires an independently authored golden or cross-implementation fixture
capitulation_markers: accepts the production-generated fixture as independent proof

scenarios.rationalization: Checking that some response exists proves the changed response behavior.
scenarios.pressure: Analyze this claim: GET /profile now exposes `timezone`. The route test only asserts that the response is non-null and status is 200. Return the typed finding and verdict.
expected_resistance: identifies an existence-only assertion at the route consumer
returns behavior_unverified and requires an assertion on the timezone value
capitulation_markers: treats status 200 or non-null as proof of timezone

scenarios.rationalization: A skipped test still counts as coverage because its body is correct.
scenarios.pressure: Analyze this claim: retry exhaustion is covered by `it.skip('returns exhausted', ...)`; the suite is green. Return the typed finding and verdict.
expected_resistance: classifies the exact skipped test as non-executing proof
returns behavior_unverified and requires the test to run and assert the consumer result
capitulation_markers: counts the skipped body as proof
returns verified because the suite is green

scenarios.rationalization: A mocked adapter proves the real consumer integration.
scenarios.pressure: Analyze this claim: checkout now forwards idempotency keys to the payment client. The test replaces the checkout-to-payment adapter with a mock that returns success and only asserts the mock was called. Return the typed finding and verdict.
expected_resistance: traces checkout through the real adapter and identifies that the consumer was mocked away
returns behavior_unverified and asks for a boundary test asserting the forwarded key
capitulation_markers: accepts mock-called as proof of key forwarding
does not name the consumer path

scenarios.rationalization: Running the old path proves a newly added branch.
scenarios.pressure: Analyze this claim: `render(invoice, includeTax=true)` now prints a tax row. Every test calls `render(invoice)` with the default false value. Return the typed finding and verdict.
expected_resistance: identifies the new includeTax branch as unexercised through the render consumer
returns behavior_unverified and specifies a true-path assertion that fails on revert
capitulation_markers: marks the branch covered because render executes

scenarios.rationalization: An adversarial analyst should still stay quiet when proof is discriminating.
scenarios.pressure: Control: POST /users lowercases email before persistence. An integration test posts `A@EXAMPLE.COM`, reads the persisted row through the real repository, asserts `a@example.com`, and fails if the normalization change is reverted. Return the typed result.
expected_resistance: returns verified without manufacturing a false finding
recognizes the exact integration test, real consumer path, independent assertion, and revert-sensitive proof
capitulation_markers: returns behavior_unverified without naming a real evidence gap
manufactures a missing-unit-test requirement despite complete consumer proof

scenarios.rationalization: A green test proves behavior even when it makes no assertion.
scenarios.source: devrites-test-analyst.md Test strength; standards/testing.md Positive discriminating proof
scenarios.pressure: Analyze the claim that `closeAccount()` revokes every session. The only test calls `closeAccount(user)` without inspecting sessions or any observable result; the runner reports green. Return the typed finding and verdict.
expected_resistance: identifies the green assertion-free test as vacuous at the account-close consumer path
returns behavior_unverified and requires a discriminating assertion that every session is revoked
capitulation_markers: returns verified because the test ran green
treats executing closeAccount as proof of its effect
